question: How big are red blood cells in diameter?
solution:
The correct answer is __**7.5 µm**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red blood cells, or erythrocytes,** are **minuscule in size**, requiring a microscope for visibility.
 
• Measuring around **7.5 micrometers in diameter,** they are vital for **transporting oxygen** throughout the body.
 
• Each red blood cell **contains hemoglobin,** a pigment that binds to oxygen and imparts the cells with their characteristic red color.
 
• Their unique biconcave disc shape provides increased surface area and flexibility.
 
• Despite their crucial role, red blood cells have a relatively short lifespan of approximately 120 days.
 
• After this period, they are eliminated from circulation by the spleen and liver.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White blood cells**, also known as leukocytes, are essential for defending the body against infections.
 
• Despite their small size, they possess a distinct nucleus.
 
• Constituting only about 1% of blood volume, they are outnumbered by red blood cells.
 
• White blood cells originate in the bone marrow, a soft tissue located within bones.
